approach:
The earlier plan is dropped. Its timeline was wrong: the producer's cargo wrapper landed on 2026-11-07 (9a97e24, first commit in HISTORY.txt to touch slot_exec.rs), so most jobs in the review window never waited on a slot. The replay also runs between producer invocations, so its time is never in `role_minutes` (status.rs:933-941). I re-derived the cause from the code and the dated history. The snapshot has no records/, so nothing below is measured; the note labels this.

Cause (read from code): 69057b9 (2026-11-06) added an unconditional line to every producer brief, `MIRROR_CHECK_INSTRUCTION` (briefs.rs:856, rendered by `mirror_check_section` at briefs.rs:640 and 863). It says: if crates/athena-cli/tests/mirrors.rs exists, run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` before you finish. athena-cli depends on agent, cap-change, cap-study, core, data, gate and git, with core's `test-support` feature and testkit as dev-dependencies (athena-cli/Cargo.toml:16-32), and an integration-test run also builds the package's binary. So the command compiles nearly the whole workspace in the test profile, in the producer's own cold target directory (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR = {job_dir}/target/{side}`, athena.toml:80,111). It applies to every job, docs-only ones included, so it shifts a median, which a trigger that fires only on some jobs would not. It sits inside the producer invocation, so `role_minutes` counts it. Since 2026-11-07 it also queues behind the build slot. The date fits: 69057b9 is 2026-11-06 and the previous review was 2026-11-04 (d0ff1e9).

The instruction duplicates two checks that already exist. The producer loop runs the same registry in-process after every report, with no build (`mirror_drift_in`, producer.rs:76, called at 361-365; a drift is sent back at 409 and 506). The configured test check runs the whole `mirrors` target at verification (decisions.md D158, Tradeoff, lines 4368-4372).

Fix: replace the instruction with a note that keeps the facts and runs no build. The facts are that a new test file needs its line in xtask/shard-timings.txt and that docs/decisions.md only gains text after its last line. The note says Athena checks both after each report, so the producer need not build to find a drift. A drift the producer misses is still sent back once by the loop, and still fails the repo test at verification.

Other candidates, in the note with the code evidence and the record that would settle each:
(a) Send-back passes: four triggers landed 2026-11-06 (10166b3 decision gate, e0f1a6f allowed paths, 69057b9 mirrors, 387255a replay), and a send-back starts a fresh session with the whole brief (agent sessions are never resumed; `session_id` is only used to remove host traces, claude.rs:386). They fire on some jobs only, so they move a median less. The record that settles it is the producer invocation count per landed job and the `self-check failed:` detail (producer.rs:434).
(b) Slot waits: only since 2026-11-07 (9a97e24).
(c) CPU contention from `max_concurrency = 2` (b32888f, 2026-11-05, athena.toml:195).
(d) Heavier readings and plans, which fits planning going from 1.7 to 9.0. That is out of scope.
The record that would confirm the chosen cause is `commands_run` of producer invocations (records.rs:712) from 2026-11-06 on, holding `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors`.

The note says plainly that the next review's window will also hold jobs that waited on slots since 2026-11-07, so the median may fall less than the fix alone would give. The boundary-scan instruction (`cargo test -p xtask --test policy`, c432163, 2026-10-27) was in both windows and is left alone.

decisions.choice: Remove the instruction to run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` from the producer brief and keep the facts it carried as a no-build note. Rename `MIRROR_CHECK_INSTRUCTION` to `MIRROR_CHECK_NOTE`; grep shows only briefs.rs uses the constant.
decisions.reason: The instruction is the one change since the previous review that adds work to every producer invocation (a cold, near-workspace-wide test build). The loop's in-process `mirror_drift_in` and the repo test at verification already catch the same drift, so the build adds time and no coverage. This removes the cause, not a symptom: no timeout, slot count, send-back limit or stage reporting changes.

rejected.option: Skip the replay in the loop on reports that get sent back (the previous plan)
rejected.why: The replay runs between producer invocations, outside `role_minutes`. It could lengthen another job's producer only through slot waits, which exist only since 2026-11-07. It does not remove what lengthened the measured window.

rejected.option: Make the instruction conditional on the planned paths touching a mirror-watched file
rejected.why: The registry (`Mirror::covers`/`watches`) lives in athena-core, and athena-context cannot depend on it. The brief is also built before any file changes. It would couple two crates for a check the loop already runs. A follow-up if the next review shows more mirror send-backs.

rejected.option: Raise or lower `max_concurrency`, `max_check_slots` or the wrapper wait cap
rejected.why: These are governance settings or symptoms (queueing and contention), the brief forbids athena.toml edits, and the slot wait did not exist for most of the window.

rejected.option: Change `role_minutes`, `StageMinutes`, the thresholds, or exclude command time from the producer stage
rejected.why: Out of scope and forbidden by criterion 4: it would hide the time. status.rs, store.rs and main.rs only sum recorded durations, so editing them could only change reporting.

rejected.option: Cut send-back triggers or raise the send-back limit
rejected.why: The trigger-by-trigger evidence is not in the snapshot. A trigger fires on some jobs only, so it fits a shifted median less. Left to a follow-up once the invocation counts per landed job are read.

risks.risk: The cause is read from code and dates, not measured: the snapshot has no records/. The mirrors test may take less time than the 10.8-minute rise, or most of the rise may come from send-back passes, slot waits or heavier plans.
risks.mitigation: The note labels the cost of the build and the share of jobs affected as estimates, lists the other candidates, and names the records that settle it (`commands_run`, invocation count per landed job, the `self-check failed:` detail). It states plainly that this job may not lower the median by the whole rise.

risks.risk: Without the instruction, a producer that adds a test file or edits the decision log and forgets the mirror gets a send-back (a fresh full pass) instead of finding it by running the target.
risks.mitigation: The brief keeps the two facts, so a careful producer avoids the drift without a build. The loop sends back what is left, and the repo test fails it at verification. The new run test shows the send-back still happens. The note records the trade, and the follow-up of a conditional instruction if the next review shows more mirror send-backs.

risks.risk: The next review's window holds slot waits (since 2026-11-07) and two-at-a-time builds, which can raise the producer median regardless of this fix.
risks.mitigation: The note names both as candidates (b) and (c), states the caveat in the section on what the next review should show, and proposes that the maintainer queue the slot-side follow-up if the median does not fall.
